chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Mug shots, and Shavers confronting Hank Jones in Chicago
summary: They went to Chicago to find a piano player and confronted Hank Jones, then club-hopped without finding one.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: had enough to get out if we paid the fine. I said, 'Well, what is -- what would bail be, Your Honor?' Then it went up to three bills and something. Well, we didn't have enough, you know, to get out on bail, so we were forced to pay the fine. But I wasn't in too much of a hurry to pay the fine. I guess that was the right thing to do, but I was just stubborn, you know. And I had plans to fight the case through the NAACP, you know. Fair practice, you know. But they didn't see this, their way. So the Judge fined us. Now, I'm looking to walk right out of the courtroom. They grabbed us by the collars and led us back behind the judge's bench and give us mug shots, you know, taking pictures, you know, with a number in front of your chest and fingerprints. I said, 'Hey, man, you're out of line.' I said, 'We paid our fine. We shouldn't be back here.' I said, 'This is a misdemeanor.' I said, 'You're going through this thing like it's a felony,' you know. He said, 'Well, we reserve the right,' you know, blah, blah, blah, to do what we want to do. He said, 'After 30 days we'll return these to you if you want them.' So we got out of jail. Charlie and I go right back to the station to go to Chicago and get a piano player, after we got out of jail. Charlie's got a checkbook and we've got our tickets, from before this happening, you know. So we go on to Chicago, and Charlie said, 'I coughed go down to the Chicago Theater and hit Hank in his mouth, for causing us to have to go through all of this.' So nothing would do but he'd

go down to the Chicago Theater, and waited for Elvin, Ray and Hank to come off the stage. And we got word to the doorman to tell Hank to come out in the alley. He came out, and we walked out on State Street, and we conversed. Charlie said, "Man, why would you leave me like that, without saying a word?" He said, "I've got a good mind to hit you in the mouth." You know, Charlie wasn't a fighter. He says -- Hank says, "Bells." And this really infuriated Charlie. Charlie said, "Come on, man, let's go, before I end up killing this man." So we went up to the Pershing Lounge and proceeded to get drunk until the clubs opened, and then we started club-hopping, and we left the next morning.
Did you actually look for a piano player?
